messages:
sanjay: hitting a weird SSL error with the python async client against our Dedicated VPC. sync client works fine though. anyone seen this?

emily: what error are you getting?

sanjay: stack trace:```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 1500, in send
    raise SSLError(exc) from exc
```

kevin: what's your config / env? base_url, cert path etc?

sanjay: using env vars + sdk default:```bash
export REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL=https://redwood.dedicated.internal
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redacted
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem
```
I also tried passing verify when creating an httpx.AsyncClient but our SDK wraps client creation so I couldn't inject it easily.

emily: does setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE help for the async client? httpx should pick up SSL_CERT_FILE in some setups but it depends on ssl.create_default_context.

sanjay: tried REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE, neither changed behavior for AsyncClient. Sync Client (requests) is fine.

jonah: probably a gap in the SDK's async constructor. We currently expose sync ca options but async path doesn't accept ca_bundle param. Can you share minimal repro?

sanjay: minimal snippet:```py
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key="redacted", base_url="https://redwood.dedicated.internal")
# expecting to pass ca_bundle but there's no kwarg
await client.generate("Hello")
```

kevin: thanks. two things to track: (1) we should add an explicit ca_bundle / trust_bundle kwarg to AsyncClient constructor that forwards to httpx's verify/ssl context, (2) make sure env var fallbacks (SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) are documented and actually honored by the async client.

emily: also note typing pain — mypy complains when people try to pass extra args because AsyncClient signature is narrow. we should update type stubs to accept Optional[str] for ca_bundle and overloads for httpx types.

jonah: UX/behaviour note: if the underlying http client raises an SSL error we probably should NOT retry by default. current retry middleware retries on transport errors and that makes things noisy in logs. add a flag retry_on_ssl = False default.

ci-bot: created issue #4521: "py-sdk: async client ca_bundle + typing + ssl-retry behavior" and linked this thread.

kevin: i'll pick this up — add param ca_bundle: str|Path|None to AsyncClient, wire to httpx.AsyncClient(verify=str(ca_bundle) or httpx.verify=...) and add unit + mypy tests. will also add a doc snippet for Dedicated/Private quickstart showing env vars and example:```bash
# recommended simple workaround until sdk fix:
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem
python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient; c=AsyncClient(api_key=\"...\", base_url=\"https://redwood.dedicated.internal\", ca_bundle=\"/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem\"); import asyncio; asyncio.run(c.generate(\"hi\"))"
```

emily: awesome — ping here when you have a draft PR so we can iterate on wording and typing. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks! that should unblock us for now.
